source.title: The extremal problems on the inertia of weighted bicyclic graphs

accepted.question_text: For a weighted bicyclic graph G_w of order n with pendant vertices, where i_+(G_w), i_-(G_w), and i_0(G_w) denote respectively the numbers of positive, negative, and zero eigenvalues in the spectrum of G_w, what are the sharp lower bounds on the positive inertia index i_+(G_w) and the negative inertia index i_-(G_w)?
accepted.context_brief: Sharp inertia lower bounds for weighted bicyclic graphs

evidence.quote: Let $G_w$ be a weighted graph. The number of the positive, negative and zero eigenvalues in the spectrum of $G_w$ are called positive inertia index, negative inertia index and nullity of $G_w$, and denoted by $i_{+}(G_w)$, $i_{-}(G_w)$, $i_{0}(G_w)$, respectively. In this paper, sharp lower bound on the positive (resp. negative) inertia index of weighted bicyclic graphs of order $n$ with pendant vertices is obtained.

accepted.question_text: For weighted bicyclic graphs G_w of order n, where i_+(G_w), i_-(G_w), and i_0(G_w) denote respectively the numbers of positive, negative, and zero eigenvalues in the spectrum of G_w, which graphs have at most two positive eigenvalues, which have at most two negative eigenvalues, and which have at least n - 4 zero eigenvalues?
accepted.context_brief: Classification of small-inertia weighted bicyclic graphs

evidence.quote: Let $G_w$ be a weighted graph. The number of the positive, negative and zero eigenvalues in the spectrum of $G_w$ are called positive inertia index, negative inertia index and nullity of $G_w$, and denoted by $i_{+}(G_w)$, $i_{-}(G_w)$, $i_{0}(G_w)$, respectively. Moreover, all the weighted bicyclic graphs of order $n$ with at most two positive, two negative and at least $n-4$ zero eigenvalues are identified, respectively.
